analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: HF Exposure to Mag 7 at the Highs, Large Bank Earnings, ASML and Anthropic Today, US Equity Positioning is a Tailwind, HF Performance in September
key_insights: GS PB data show hedge fund net exposure to the Mag 7 at the highs, even though overall net risk is low. Mag 7 has outperformed the NDX for 8 straight sessions. 3-month implied volatility is near the lows, so longs have a cheap chance to add hedges.

Morgan Stanley's headline beat came from equities trading ($5.8bn vs $4.9bn consensus), which more than offset a FICC miss, and from net interest income (NII) up in the high teens vs consensus. Wealth flows were strong: ~$80bn fee-based and $232bn total. The miss was in wealth pre-tax income and margin, which looks like higher wealth compensation as a share of revenue. CET1 was flat at 14.9% with a ~$1.5bn buyback. The stock is down 17% since mid-July.

Bank of America missed PPNR by 4%, driven mainly by trading, which fell ~5.5% YoY against guidance of roughly flat. Equities and FICC both missed, with FICC down 17% YoY. Investment banking was a slight beat on debt underwriting but fees missed overall. Expenses were in line, producing -370bps of operating leverage. NII was ~30bps better than expected. Buybacks were $6bn, TCE/TA was about 6% and CET1 fell 40bps.

Bank of America's call focus: why trading is weak vs peers, expense levers if fees stay weak (including whether last night's money laundering fine remediation is already in the expense base), and the NII guide. Bulls want an NII guide-up given the more hawkish rate environment.

ASML is fading on results despite a Q3 beat and raise and signaled upside to its 2028+ long-term unit guidance. Bears point to the lack of upgrades to 2027 capacity. The 2pm call is key. Hedge funds are supplying stock.
AI sentiment has weakened on concerns over power and funding constraints, uncertain returns, rising model competition, and custom silicon reducing reliance on leading GPU suppliers.

Anthropic is holding an investor event in San Francisco today and will release updated financials to institutional investors. Watch ARR figures after OpenAI lowered its ARR last week from $70bn to $50bn.

Other tech moves: CRWV -4% on social media focus on bond yields spiking and private credit bubble warnings. HPE, NTAP and DELL fell on Barclays downgrades. MU and SNDK were lower in 8 of 9 sessions. GOOGL +1% on the Gemini 4 Argon release.

US equity positioning is a moderate tailwind. Corporate buybacks may be met by mutual fund selling into their October year-end, and will soon be joined by positive retail flows and a foreign investor bid after the midterms. November is the 2nd highest month for corporate repurchases on the GS desk.

Foreign inflows have historically reached about 1.75% of AUM in the six months after midterm elections. November and December see consecutive positive inflows, rivaled only by Feb-Mar. In the tail scenarios for bonds, CTAs turn buyers, and the asymmetry for the S&P 500 is firmly to the downside.

Hedge funds were flat globally in September. Systematic Macro/CTA funds led at +3.8%, the strategy's best month this year and best YTD. Short fixed income and long energy were key contributors. Quant funds also gained on short-side momentum. Fundamental strategies lagged and Asia was the only positive region.
